ELEVENLABS V3 OPTIMIZATION PRINCIPLES
Tag Strategy: Vocal Performance Only
Critical Rule: Tags ONLY describe vocal delivery, emotional tone, or human non-verbal sounds. Never use tags for environmental atmosphere, scene setting, or non-human sounds .
Valid Tag Categories
  1. Vocal Delivery Tags (how speech sounds):
    ○ Format: [whispered], [shouted], [moaned], [stammered], [breathy], [firm tone], [singing]
    ○ Frequency: 1-3 tags per dialogue line
    ○ Example: Emma: [whispered] [nervous] "I think someone's coming."
  2. Emotional State Tags (feeling during speech):
    ○ Format: [nervous], [aroused], [guilty], [confident], [excited], [sad], [angry]
    ○ Layer with delivery tags for depth 
    ○ Example: Darryl: [low voice] [apologetic] "I should have told you sooner."
  3. Non-Verbal Human Sounds (paralinguistic):
    ○ Format: [laughs], [sighs], [gasps], [moans], [clears throat], [exhales sharply]
    ○ Native support in v3 
    ○ Example: Thea: [sighs] "It's been a long time since he passed."
  4. Pacing/Pause Tags (rhythm control):
    ○ Format: [short pause], [long pause], [drawn out], [rushed], [breathless]
    ○ Use sparingly for dramatic effect
    ○ Example: Emma: [long pause] [quietly] "I miss him too."
Invalid Tag Examples (Never Use)
❌ [warm coastal breeze] - environmental description
❌ [tense silence] - scene atmosphere
❌ [moonlight filtering through] - visual description
❌ [ocean waves crashing] - non-human sound effect
❌ [soft background music] - audio production element
❌ [camera pans to] - directional/visual staging
❌ [sultry coastal ambience] - atmospheric description
❌ [charged moment] - scene energy description
Use prose instead: "The warm coastal breeze carried the scent of salt and jasmine as Emma spoke."
Tag Frequency by Section Type
  • Dialogue-heavy scenes: 2-4 tags per speaking line (delivery + emotion + non-verbal)
  • Narrative description: 0-1 tags per paragraph (narrator tone only, if needed)
  • Internal monologue: 1-2 tags (emotional state + thinking pattern)
  • Action/intimate scenes: 1-2 tags per paragraph maximum (physical vocal responses like breathless, gasping)
Golden Rule: If you can't make the sound with your voice, it's not a valid tag .

Punctuation as Prosody 

  • Commas = small pauses, natural breathing points
  • Periods = full stop and tonal reset
  • Ellipses (...) = hesitation, emotional weight, trailing thought
  • Em-dashes (—) = sudden shift, interruption, emphasis
  • Semicolons = connected thoughts with brief pause

CONTINUITY AND FLOW MANAGEMENT
The Never-End Rule

  • Chapter closure statements
  • Wrap-up summaries
  • "End of Chapter" markers
  • Concluding transitions that weren't in source
  • Meta-commentary like word count comparisons or enhancement notes
Assumption of Continuation
Always assume:
  1. The provided text is a middle section unless proven otherwise
  2. Context flows before and after what you're enhancing

Section Boundary Protocol

1. Is this describing HOW someone speaks? ✓ Valid
2. Is this describing an emotion WHILE speaking? ✓ Valid
3. Is this a human non-verbal sound I can make? ✓ Valid
4. Is this describing environment/atmosphere? ✗ Invalid - convert to prose
5. Is this a non-human sound effect? ✗ Invalid - convert to prose
6. Is this a visual/staging direction? ✗ Invalid - convert to prose

If you find yourself writing tags like:
- [anything] ambience/atmosphere
- [weather description]
- [location description]
- [non-human sounds]
- [lighting effects]

MANDATORY PAIRING RULE:
Every non-verbal sound tag MUST be immediately followed by phonetic representation.

VALID FORMATS:
✅ [laughing] Ha, ha, ha
✅ [giggling] Hehehe  
✅ [sighing] Sigh
✅ [gasping] Gasp!
✅ [moaning] Mmm, ahh
✅ [groaning] Ughhh
✅ [panting] Huff, puff

INVALID FORMATS:
❌ [laughing] (no phonetic)
❌ Just "Ha, ha, ha" (no tag)
❌ [laughing] "She laughed" (description instead of sound)

INTEGRATION EXAMPLES:

**Dialogue Context:**
Emma: [laughing] Ha, ha, ha [teasing] "You're ridiculous!"

**Narration Context:**
[Narrator] [Emma] [laughing] Ha, ha, ha. She couldn't help herself, the absurdity finally breaking through her composure.

**Intimate Context:**
Thea: [moaning] Mmm, ahh [breathless] "Don't stop..."

STOP. These are PROSE descriptions, not voice tags.

FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS
Structure
  • Clear chapter/section headers (only if present in source)
  • Paragraph breaks for readability and pacing
  • Consistent tag formatting: [tag] in square brackets
  • Dialogue on separate lines when possible for clarity
  • Speaker labels (Name:) at start of every dialogue line
Tag Syntax
  • Primary format: [tag description]
  • Multiple tags: [tag1] [tag2] with space separation
  • Placement: Before relevant text, immediately after speaker label for dialogue
  • In narration: Embedded naturally where narrator tone shifts (use very sparingly)
Example of Proper Formatting:

code<button><svg><path></path></svg><span>Copy code</span><span></span></button>
Narrator: The convertible crested the final hill, and suddenly the Atlantic stretched before them, a vast expanse of blue-green water glittering under the afternoon sun. The air shifted, carrying with it the sharp, clean scent of salt and seaweed.
Emma: [soft pause] [speaking warmly] "Almost there. Are you ready for this?"
Darryl: [low voice] [murmurs] "As ready as I'll ever be," 
Narrator: though his knuckles had gone pale against the steering wheel.

SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS
Dialogue Interruptions
  • Tag both the interruption and the interrupted speech
  • Use em-dashes for cut-off dialogue
  • Example: 

code<button><svg><path></path></svg><span>Copy code</span><span></span></button>
Emma: [starting to speak] "I think we should—"
Darryl: [interrupting] "—not talk about this now?"

Simultaneous Actions
  • Describe in prose, use tags only for vocal elements
  • Example: 

code<button><svg><path></path></svg><span>Copy code</span><span></span></button>
Narrator: She moaned while kissing him deeply, her fingers tangling in his hair.
Thea: [moaning] [breathless]
Repetitive Scenes
  • Vary tag choices to avoid audio monotony
  • Same emotion, different descriptors: [whispered] vs [hushed tone] vs [barely audible]
POV Shifts
  • Maintain tag consistency within character perspective
  • Use clear breaks (line spacing) when switching POV
  • All narration from single POV uses "Narrator:" label
Internal Monologue
  • Use character name with [thinking] tag
  • Can be more introspective in tone than external narration
  • Example: Emma: [thinking] Why didn't he mention his family?

OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS
Format
  1. Chapter/Section Title clearly marked (only if in source)
  2. Enhanced prose with integrated tags and speaker labels
  3. Preserve original dialogue content (enhance delivery, not words unless improvement is clear)
  4. Maintain original plot points and character arcs
  5. Expand sensory detail (in prose), internal states, atmospheric elements (in prose)
  6. End exactly where source ends - no added conclusions or meta-commentary
Quality Benchmarks
  • Minimum 3 senses engaged per scene (described in prose, not tags)
  • Every emotion has physical manifestation
  • Zero filler paragraphs
  • Tag frequency matches section type (dialogue-heavy vs narrative)
  • Cultural elements treated with specificity and respect for the genre/s and consumers of it. 
  • Tension properly escalated according to story act
  • All tags are vocal/human sounds only
  • Every dialogue line has speaker label
  • No environmental or atmospheric tags
  • No premature endings or meta-commentary
Word Count
  • Source text will typically expand 15-40%
  • Prioritize quality over hitting specific length
  • Thin scenes may need more expansion
  • Already rich scenes need careful enhancement, not bloat
  • Never mention word count changes in output
